info.name: AudioEffect
info.comment: Support class for processors attached to an Audio mixing chain.

description.p: AudioEffect is a support class for audio processors. Use a derived class to perform DSP; the AudioEffect class itself passes samples through unchanged.

A zero Channel applies the effect universally. Otherwise use the complete handle returned by Audio.OpenChannels(). Application chains process their channel set before it is added to the master mix. The global chain processes the master mix before the built-in output filter. Lower Order values run first; ties retain attachment order.

Attachment, field changes and detachment are serialised with mixing. Freeing an effect waits for any current mix window before detaching it. Closing its channel set or freeing its Audio target disconnects the effect; a disconnected effect must be replaced to attach it again. Global effects are immutable after initialisation.
Subclasses can publish their parameters in the Schema field, so that a client can present and change any effect without knowing its class. The schema is an XML document:
description.pre: <effect class="AudioEqualiser" version="1" description="A parametric equaliser."> <param key="gain" label="Output Trim" type="double" unit="dB" scale="linear" min="-48" max="48" default="0"/> <group key="bands" label="Band" min="0" max="64"> <param key="type" label="Type" type="enum" default="0"> <option value="0" key="peak" label="Peak" description="Boosts or cuts a range."/> </param> <param key="q" label="Q" type="double" scale="log" min="0.1" max="20" default="0.707"> <rule key="type" values="1,2" max="1"/> </param> </group> <output key="response" type="curve"/> </effect>
description.p: The effect, group, param and option elements may carry a description attribute. It contains one or more complete sentences that explain the item's purpose in terms suitable for presentation to the user, e.g. as a tooltip. The attribute is omitted if no description is available.

A param element describes one value. Its type is double, int, bool or enum; enumerations list their values as option elements. The unit attribute is omitted for unitless values. The scale is linear or log and indicates how a control should map positions to values. The min and max bounds are inclusive unless min-exclusive or max-exclusive is set. A max of nyquist means half of the OutputRate and is always exclusive. A step is present only for stepped values.

A group element describes a repeated structure, such as a list of equaliser bands, with min and max entry counts. Its entries are numbered from zero. Use GetGroupCount to read the number of entries, including staged insertions and removals.

A rule element relates a parameter to a sibling in the same group, or to another top-level parameter. If the sibling named by key holds one of the listed values, the parameter is either ignored by the processor (inactive="1") or limited to a lower max.
An output element names data that can be read back from the processor. A curve output is read with GetResponse.

Parameters are addressed by key-paths: key for a top-level parameter, or group[index].key for a group member, e.g. bands[2].frequency. Values are always in real units, such as hertz or decibels; they are never normalised.

Before initialisation, SetParameter, InsertEntry and RemoveEntry change the effect directly and Init() validates the result. After initialisation they change a working copy instead, which is applied as a single change when the client calls Flush(). This allows related changes, such as switching a band's type together with its Q, without the processor ever running the state between them. GetParameter reports staged values. A flush that breaks any rule is rejected in full and the working copy is discarded.

action.name: Flush
action.comment: Applies changes staged by SetParameter(), InsertEntry() and RemoveEntry().

description.p: After initialisation, parameter changes made through SetParameter, InsertEntry and RemoveEntry are held in a working copy. Flush() validates the working copy as a whole and applies it in a single step, so the processor never runs a partially changed state.

The working copy is discarded whether or not the flush succeeds. If any value or rule is invalid, the effect is left unchanged and ERR::InvalidValue is returned. Calling Flush() with no staged changes has no effect.

result.error: The staged changes were applied, or there were none.
The effect has been disconnected from its Audio object.
The staged changes break a rule or range. Nothing was applied.
The effect is attached to the global chain.

method.name: GetGroupCount
method.comment: Reads the number of entries in a parameter group.
method.prototype: ERR fx::GetGroupCount(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Group, INT * Count)

input.param: The group key published in Schema, e.g. bands.
The number of entries is returned here.

description.p: Returns the current entry count for the named group. Staged insertions and removals are included, matching GetParameter. A failed Flush() discards staged changes, so subsequent queries return the committed count. The count can be read before initialisation or after the effect has been disconnected.

result.error: Operation successful.
The group is unknown.
The effect does not publish a schema.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: GetParameter
method.comment: Reads a parameter value by key.
method.prototype: ERR fx::GetParameter(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Path, DOUBLE * Value)

input.param: A parameter key such as gain or bands[2].frequency.
The parameter value is returned here.

description.p: Reads the value of a parameter published in the Schema. If changes are staged, the staged value is returned, so a client always reads back what it has set. Enumerated values are returned as their numeric value.

result.error: Operation successful.
The key is malformed or names an unknown parameter.
The effect does not publish a schema.
The group index does not refer to an existing entry.
Function call missing argument value(s)

method.name: GetResponse
method.prototype: ERR fx::GetResponse(OBJECTPTR Object, std::span<const double> Frequencies, std::span<double> Magnitudes)

input.param: Frequencies in hertz. Each must be above zero and below half of the OutputRate.
Receives the response in decibels. Must be the same length as Frequencies.

description.p: Computes the response of the effect at each of the given frequencies, in decibels, from its committed parameters at the current OutputRate. Staged changes are not included. Effects that support this method list an output of type curve in their Schema.

result.error: Operation successful.
The arrays are empty, of different lengths, or longer than 4096 entries.
The effect does not compute a response.
The output rate is not yet known.
Function call missing argument value(s)
A frequency is not above zero and below half of the output rate.

method.name: InsertEntry
method.comment: Inserts a new entry into a parameter group.
method.prototype: ERR fx::InsertEntry(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Group, INT Index)

input.param: The key of the group, e.g. bands.
The zero-based position for the new entry.

description.p: Inserts an entry at Index, filled with the default values published in the Schema. Later entries move up by one. Set Index to the current entry count to append. After initialisation the insertion is staged until Flush() is called.

result.error: Operation successful.
The group is unknown.
The effect does not publish a schema.
The index is invalid or the group is full.
The effect has been disconnected from its Audio object.
Function call missing argument value(s)
The effect is attached to the global chain.

method.name: RemoveEntry
method.comment: Removes an entry from a parameter group.
method.prototype: ERR fx::RemoveEntry(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Group, INT Index)

input.param: The key of the group, e.g. bands.
The zero-based position of the entry to remove.

description.p: Removes the entry at Index. Later entries move down by one and keep their processing state. After initialisation the removal is staged until Flush() is called.

result.error: Operation successful.
The group is unknown.
The effect does not publish a schema.
The index is invalid or the group is at its minimum size.
The effect has been disconnected from its Audio object.
Function call missing argument value(s)
The effect is attached to the global chain.

method.name: SetParameter
method.comment: Changes a parameter value by key.
method.prototype: ERR fx::SetParameter(OBJECTPTR Object, STRVIEW Path, DOUBLE Value)

input.param: A parameter key such as gain or bands[2].frequency.
The new value, in the parameter's unit.

description.p: Sets a parameter published in the Schema. The value is checked against the parameter's own range immediately. Rules that relate parameters to each other are checked when the change is applied: by Init() before initialisation, or by Flush() afterwards. After initialisation the change is staged and has no effect on the processor until Flush() is called.
Enumerated values are set with their numeric value.

result.error: Operation successful.
The key is malformed or names an unknown parameter.
The effect does not publish a schema.
The group index does not refer to an existing entry.
The effect has been disconnected from its Audio object.
Function call missing argument value(s)
The value is outside the parameter's range.
The effect is attached to the global chain.

field.name: Audio
field.comment: Target Audio object, inherited from an Audio owner if omitted.

description.p: Set before initialisation. Explicit targets take precedence over ownership. Ownership changes after attachment do not change the target. Freeing the target disconnects all its effects, including effects owned by other objects.

field.name: Channel
field.comment: Channel-set handle, or zero for the global chain.

description.p: Set before initialisation. Use the complete handle returned by Audio.OpenChannels(), with a zero low word. Individual channel handles and closed channel sets are rejected.

field.name: Mutable
field.comment: Read-only. Zero if the effect's parameters can no longer be changed.

description.p: Returns zero for an initialised effect in the global chain or an initialised effect disconnected from its Audio object or channel set. Otherwise returns one.
Lower values run first. Ties resolve by original attachment order, including after an application effect is reordered. Global effects cannot change order after initialisation.

field.name: OutputRate
field.comment: Read-only output sample rate of the attached Audio object.

description.p: Updated when the Audio device is activated. Processors reset before processing the new output configuration.

field.name: Schema
field.comment: Read-only. An XML description of the effect's parameters.

description.p: The schema describes every parameter that can be read or changed with GetParameter and SetParameter, including units, ranges, defaults, repeated groups and the rules between parameters. The format is described in the class documentation. The schema is the same for every instance of a class; instance-specific bounds, such as the Nyquist frequency, are resolved against OutputRate.
The value is empty if the class does not publish a schema.

field.name: Stereo
field.comment: Read-only output layout; one for stereo and zero for mono.

description.p: Updated on device activation together with OutputRate.

constants.const: Skip an application effect. Global effects cannot be bypassed.
